name: service-readiness-registry
purpose: Defines production-service readiness gates for the installable desktop platform so internal builds, customer test builds, and public releases are not confused.

reader_guide.summary: Use this registry when deciding whether the desktop platform is a local/internal build, a controlled customer-test build, or ready for public service release signoff.
how_to_read: Read service_levels first to understand which claims are allowed.
Read readiness_groups to see the grouped service gaps that must be visible in the app.
Read public_release_blockers before using public release language.
Read runtime_surface_contract to understand what the installed app must show to operators.
Treat updater, signing, notarization, privacy, support, and first-run items as release gates rather than optional notes.
update_triggers: A release channel, updater, signing, notarization, support, privacy, or onboarding behavior changes.
The app starts collecting additional logs, workspace data, or diagnostics.
A customer-test or public distribution claim is made.
A new OS packaging target is added.

structure_rules.rule: A local/internal app bundle may be useful for development, but it must not be described as a public service release until public release blockers are cleared.
structure_rules.reason: Developer ID signing, notarization, updater configuration, and clean-machine smoke tests are trust gates for installed software.

structure_rules.rule: Release, updater, privacy, support, onboarding, and workspace-readiness gaps must be visible in the app surface, not only in docs.
structure_rules.reason: A real service needs operators to see next actions and blockers without reading repository internals.

structure_rules.rule: Support diagnostics must export bounded metadata and redacted summaries, not raw private workspace contents or secrets.
structure_rules.reason: Customer support workflows can accidentally become data exfiltration paths if raw logs or source trees are bundled.

structure_rules.rule: A public service release requires a documented update and rollback path. Until a signed updater or equivalent release channel is configured, public release remains blocked.
structure_rules.reason: Installed customers need a safe path for security fixes and product updates.

service_levels.label: Local/Internal Build
service_levels.allowed_claim: Useful for development and internal smoke testing.

service_levels.label: Customer Test Build
service_levels.allowed_claim: Installable pilot build for controlled testers with known limitations.

readiness_groups.label: Runtime Data Boundary
readiness_groups.intent: Runtime data, logs, task runs, support bundles, and agent workspace must live outside the platform source tree.

readiness_groups.label: Native Resource Telemetry
readiness_groups.intent: The installed desktop app must expose Rust/Tauri process memory, CPU, system memory, and workspace cache state so desktop resource usage is visible and auditable.

readiness_groups.label: Customer Payload
readiness_groups.intent: The installed app must not bundle platform source trees, private vaults, development outputs, or raw repository snapshots.

readiness_groups.label: Support Diagnostics
readiness_groups.intent: Operators must be able to export redacted diagnostics for support and recovery.

readiness_groups.label: Provider Accounts
readiness_groups.intent: Provider credential status, local Ollama model catalog readiness, and direct model-task execution readiness must be visible in the app, while credential reports and support exports stay redacted.

readiness_groups.label: Workspace Onboarding
readiness_groups.intent: Customers need a first-run workspace chooser and clear setup state before running agents.

readiness_groups.label: Privacy & Logging
readiness_groups.intent: Logs and diagnostics must preserve provenance, bounds, redaction, and sensitive-data rules.

readiness_groups.label: Signed Distribution
readiness_groups.intent: macOS public distribution requires Developer ID signing, hardened runtime, notarization, and stapling when applicable.

readiness_groups.label: Update & Recovery
readiness_groups.intent: Public service releases need a signed update channel, rollback notes, and clean-machine smoke tests.

readiness_groups.label: Production Agent Blueprints
readiness_groups.intent: Expose AgentCore-style runtime, memory, gateway, and evaluation blueprints as local-first desktop agent creation and task-run controls while keeping Python agent execution local and AWS deployment optional.
checks: AgentCore blueprint UI exists in the Agents screen
Blueprint application fills runnable search-agent and Agent Core inputs
AgentCore Quick Builder can create an Agent Core proposal record through the native proposal writer
Agent proposal records declare local Python execution and local process runtime as the host boundary
Reference registry records AWS AgentCore docs and awslabs/agentcore-samples public-source boundary
AWS AgentCore CLI and AWS credentials are treated as optional deployment adapter readiness, not required local runtime setup or the execution host

public_release_blockers: Developer ID signing identity or APPLE_CERTIFICATE credentials are not configured.
Apple notarization credentials are not configured.
Signed updater channel is not configured.
Clean-machine install/open/update smoke test has not been recorded.

runtime_surface_contract.desktop_panel: Workspace Monitor Desktop shall show Service Readiness with grouped status, score, blockers, warnings, and next actions.
